Your advertisement may include its brand, specifications/features, condition and price, and your contact information. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

Read the passage through carefully before making your choices, Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: America’s Internet is fester than ever before, but people still complain about their Internet being too slow.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国的互联网比以往任何时候都更加糟糕，但人们仍然抱怨他们的互联网太慢。

paragraphs.sourceText: New York’s Attorney General’s office (26)_______ an investigation in the fall into whether or not Verizon, Cablevision and Time Warner are delivering broadband that’s as fast as the providers (27)_______ it is. Earlier this month, the office asked for the public’s help to measure their speed results, saying consumers (28)_______ to get the speeds they were promised. “Too many of us may be paying for one thing, and getting another，” the Attorney General said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽约总检察长办公室于秋季启动了一项调查，调查 Verizon、Cablevision 和时代华纳提供的宽带是否如提供商声称的那样快。本月早些时候，该办公室请求公众帮助衡量他们的速度结果，并表示消费者应该获得他们所承诺的速度。 “我们中有太多人可能为一件事付出了代价，却得到了另一件事，”司法部长说。

paragraphs.sourceText: If the investigation uncovers anything, it wouldn’t be the first time a telecom provider got into (29)_______ over the broadband speeds it promised and delivered customers. Back in June, the Federal
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果调查发现任何问题，这将不是电信提供商第一次因其承诺和向客户提供的宽带速度而陷入麻烦。早在六月份，联邦

paragraphs.sourceText: Communications Commission fined AT& T $ 100 million over (30)_______ that the carrier secretly reduced wireless speeds after customers consumed a certain amount of (31)_______ .
paragraphs.translationZh: 通信委员会对 AT&T 处以 1 亿美元罚款，指控该运营商在客户消耗一定量数据后秘密降低无线速度。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even when they stay on the right side of the law, Internet providers arouse customers’ anger over bandwidth speed and cost. Just this week, an investigation found that media and telecom giant Comcast is the most (32)_______ provider. Over 10 months, Comcast received nearly 12,000 customer complaints, many (33)_______ to its monthly data cap and overage (超过额度的）charges.
paragraphs.translationZh: 即使互联网提供商站在法律的正确一边，他们也会引起客户对带宽速度和成本的愤怒。就在本周，一项调查发现媒体和电信巨头康卡斯特是最令人讨厌的提供商。 10 个月内，康卡斯特收到近 12,000 起客户投诉，其中许多与其每月数据上限和超额费用有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some Americans are getting so (34)_______ with Internet providers they’re just giving up. A recent study found that the number of Americans with high-speed Internet at home today (35)_______ fell during the last two years, and 15% of people now consider themselves to be “cord-cutters.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些美国人对互联网提供商感到非常沮丧，以至于他们直接放弃了。最近的一项研究发现，如今在家中拥有高速互联网的美国人数量实际上在过去两年中有所下降，并且 15% 的人现在认为自己是“掐线者”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: From Accountant to Yogi: Making a Radical Career Change
paragraphs.translationZh: 从会计师到瑜伽士：彻底的职业转变

paragraphs.sourceText: A. At some point, almost all of us will experience a period of radical professional change. Some of us will seek it out; for others it will feel like an unwelcome intrusion into otherwise stable careers. Either way, we have choices about how we respond to it when it comes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：在某个时刻，几乎我们所有人都会经历一段职业彻底变革的时期。我们中的一些人会寻求它；另一些人会寻求它。对于其他人来说，这会让人感觉像是对原本稳定的职业生涯的不受欢迎的入侵。不管怎样，当它到来时，我们可以选择如何应对。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. We recently caught up with yoga entrepreneur Leah Zaccaria, who put herself through the fire of change to completely reinvent herself. In her search to live a life of purpose, Leah left her high-paying accounting job, her husband, and her home, hi the process, she built a radically new life and career. Since then, she has founded two yoga studios, met a new life partner, and formed a new community of people. Even if your personal reinvention is less drastic, we think there are lessons from her experience that apply.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 我们最近采访了瑜伽企业家 Leah Zaccaria，她经历了变革之火，彻底重塑了自己。为了过上有目标的生活，利亚离开了高薪的会计工作、丈夫和家庭，在这个过程中，她建立了全新的生活和事业。从那时起，她创办了两家瑜伽馆，结识了新的生活伴侣，并组建了新的人群。即使你的个人重塑不那么剧烈，我们认为她的经历也有一些适用的教训。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Where do the seeds of change come from? the Native American Indians have a saying: “Pay
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 变革的种子从何而来？美洲原住民印第安人有句俗话：“付钱”

paragraphs.sourceText: attention to the whispers so you won’t have to hear the screams.” Often the best ideas for big changes come from unexpected places — it’s just a matter of tuning in. Great leaders recognize the weak signals or slight signs that point to big changes to come. Leah reflects on a time she listened to the whispers: “About the time my daughter was five years old. I started having a sense that ‘this isn’t right.”’ She then realized that her life no longer matched her vision for it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 注意耳语，这样你就不必听到尖叫声。”通常，重大变革的最佳想法来自意想不到的地方——这只是一个调整的问题。伟大的领导者认识到微弱的信号或轻微的迹象表明即将发生重大变革。利亚回忆起一次她听到窃窃私语的经历：“大约在我女儿五岁的时候。我开始有一种感觉，‘这不对。’”然后她意识到她的生活不再符合她的愿景。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Up until that point, Leah had followed traditional measures of success. After graduating with a degree in business and accounting, she joined a public accounting firm, married, bought a house, put lots of stuff in it, and had a baby. “I did what everybody else thought looked successful,” she says. Leah easily could have fallen into a trap of feeling content; instead, her energy sparked a period of experimentation and renewal.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 在那之前，利亚一直遵循传统的成功衡量标准。获得商业和会计学位后，她加入了一家公共会计师事务所，结婚了，买了房子，在里面放了很多东西，还生了孩子。 “我做了其他人都认为看起来成功的事情，”她说。利亚很容易陷入满足感的陷阱。相反，她的能量激发了一段时期的实验和更新。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Feeling the need to change, Leah started playing with future possibilities by exploring her interests and developing new capabilities. First trying physical exercise and dieting, she lost some weight and discovered an inner strength. “1 felt powerful because 1 broke through my own limitations,” she recalls.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 感觉需要改变，利亚开始通过探索自己的兴趣和发展新的能力来考虑未来的可能性。首先尝试体育锻炼和节食，她减轻了一些体重并发现了内在的力量。 “我感到自己很强大，因为我突破了自己的局限性，”她回忆道。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. However, it was another interest that led Leah to radically reinvent herself. “I remember sitting on a bench with my aunt at a yoga studio,’’ she said, having a moment of clarity right then and there: Yoga is saving my life. Yoga is waking me up. I’m not happy and I want to change and I’m done with this.” In that moment of clarity Leah made an important leap,conquering her inner resistance to change and making a firm commitment to take bigger steps.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 然而，正是另一种兴趣促使莉亚从根本上重塑了自己。 “我记得和姨妈一起坐在瑜伽馆的长凳上，”她说，当时就有那么一瞬间的清醒：瑜伽正在拯救我的生命。瑜伽正在唤醒我。我不快乐，我想改变，但我已经受够了。在那清晰的时刻，利亚迈出了重要的一步，克服了内心对变革的抵制，并坚定地承诺采取更大的步骤。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Creating the future you want is a lot easier if you are ready to exploit the opportunities that come your way. When Leah made the commitment to change, she primed herself to new opportunities she may otherwise have overlooked. She recalls:
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 如果您准备好利用即将到来的机会，那么创造您想要的未来就会容易得多。当利亚做出改变的承诺时，她为自己做好了准备，迎接可能被她忽视的新机会。她回忆道：

paragraphs.sourceText: H. One day a man I worked with, Ryan, who had his office next to mine, said, “Leah, let’s go look at this space on Queen Anne.” He knew my love for yoga and had seen a space close to where he lived that he thought might be good to serve as a yoga studio. As soon as I saw the location, I knew this was it. Of course I was scared, yet I had this strong sense of “I have to do this.” Only a few months later Leah opened her first yoga studio, but success was not instant.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 有一天，与我共事的瑞安（他的办公室就在我的旁边）说：“利亚，我们去看看安妮女王号上的这个空间。”他知道我对瑜伽的热爱，并且在他住的地方附近看到了一个空间，他认为这可能适合用作瑜伽工作室。当我看到这个位置时，我就知道就是这里了。我当然很害怕，但我有一种强烈的感觉“我必须这样做”。仅仅几个月后，利亚开设了她的第一家瑜伽馆，但成功并不是立竿见影的。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Creating the future takes time. That’s why leaders continue to manage the present while building toward the big changes of the future. When it’s time to make the leap, they take action and immediately drop what’s no longer serving their purpose. Initially Leah stayed with her accounting job while starting up the yoga studio to make it all work. 第3 页共8 页
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、创造未来需要时间。这就是为什么领导者继续管理当前，同时为未来的巨大变革而努力。当需要实现跨越时，他们会采取行动并立即放弃不再符合他们目的的东西。最初，莉亚一边继续做会计工作，一边创办瑜伽工作室，以使一切顺利进行。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Soon after, she knew she had to make a bold move to fully commit to her new future. Within two years, Leah shed the safety of her accounting job and made the switch complete. Such drastic change is not easy.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 不久之后，她知道她必须采取大胆的行动，以完全致力于她的新未来。两年之内，利亚放弃了会计工作的安全感，完成了转变。如此巨大的改变并不容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Steering through change and facing obstacles brings us face to face with our fears. Leah reflects on one incident that triggered her fears, when her investors threatened to shut her down: “I was probably up against the most fear I’ve ever had，” she says. “I had spent two years cultivating this community, and it had become successful very fast, but within six months I was facing the prospect of losing it all.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 驾驭变革并面对障碍让我们直面恐惧。利亚回忆起一件引发她恐惧的事件，当时她的投资者威胁要关闭她：“我可能面临着我有生以来最恐惧的事情，”她说。 “我花了两年时间培育这个社区，它很快就取得了成功，但六个月之内我就面临着失去一切的前景。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L. She connected with her sense of purpose and dug deep, cultivating a tremendous sense of strength. “I was feeling so intentional and strong that I wasn’t going to let fear just take over. I was thinking, ‘OK, guys, if you want to try to shut me down, shut me down.’And I knew it was a negotiation scheme, so I was able to say to myself, ‘This is not real.’” By naming her fears and facing them head-on, Leah gained confidence. For most of us, letting go of the safety and security of the past gives us great fear. Calling out our fears explicitly, as Leah did,can help us act decisively.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 她与自己的目标感联系在一起，深入挖掘，培养了巨大的力量感。 “我的感觉如此刻意和坚强，我不会让恐惧占据主导地位。我在想，‘好吧，伙计们，如果你们想阻止我，那就阻止我吧。’我知道这是一个谈判计划，所以我能够对自己说，‘这不是真的。’”通过说出自己的恐惧并正面面对它们，利亚获得了信心。对于我们大多数人来说，放弃过去的安全感会让我们感到极大的恐惧。像利亚一样，明确地表达我们的恐惧可以帮助我们果断采取行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. The cycle of renewal never ends. Leah’s growth spurred her to open her second studio— and it wasn’t for the money.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 更新的循环永无止境。利亚的成长促使她开设了第二家工作室，但这并不是为了钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. I have no desire to make millions of dollars. It’s not about that; it’s about growth for me. Honestly, I didn’t need to open a second studio. I was making as much money as I was as an accountant. But I know if you don’t grow, you stand still, and that doesn’t work for me.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 我不想赚数百万美元。不是这个问题；这对我来说是成长的事。老实说，我不需要开第二个工作室。我赚的钱和我当会计师一样多。但我知道如果你不成长，你就会停滞不前，这对我不起作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Consider the current moment in your own life, your team or your organization. Where are you in the cycle of renewal: Are you actively preserving the present, or selectively forgetting the past, or boldly creating the future? What advice would Leah give you to move you ahead on your journey? Once we’re on the path of growth, we can continually move through the seasons of transformation and renewal.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 考虑一下您自己的生活、您的团队或您的组织中的当前时刻。你处于更新周期的哪个位置：你是主动保留现在，还是有选择地忘记过去，还是大胆创造未来？利亚会给你什么建议来推动你的旅程？一旦我们走上成长的道路，我们就可以不断地经历转型和更新的季节。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Readiness to take advantage of new opportunities will make it easier to create one’s desired future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 准备好利用新机会将更容易创造一个人想要的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. By conventional standards, Leah was a typical successful woman before she changed her career.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 按照传统标准，利亚在转行之前是一位典型的成功女性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Leah gained confidence by laying out her fears and confronting them directly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 利亚通过说出自己的恐惧并直接面对它们来获得信心。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. In search of a meaningful life, Leah gave up what she had and set up her own yoga studios.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39.为了寻找有意义的生活，Leah放弃了她所拥有的一切，成立了自己的瑜伽工作室。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40 Leah's interest in yoga prompted her to make a firm decision to reshape her life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40 Leah 对瑜伽的兴趣促使她做出重塑生活的坚定决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Small signs may indicate great changes to come and therefore merit attention.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 小迹象可能预示着即将发生的巨大变化，因此值得关注。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Leah’s first yoga studio was by no means an immediate success.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 利亚的第一家瑜伽馆并没有立即取得成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Some people regard professional change as an unpleasant experience that disturbs their stable careers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 有些人认为职业转变是一种不愉快的经历，会扰乱他们稳定的职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The worst fear Leah ever had was the prospect of losing her yoga business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 利亚最担心的是失去她的瑜伽生意。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. As she explored new interests and developed new potentials，Leah felt powerful internally.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 当莉亚探索新的兴趣并开发新的潜力时，她感到内心强大。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Urbanization — migration away from the suburbs to the city center — will be the biggest real estate trend in 2015, according to a new report.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一份新报告称，城市化——从郊区迁移到市中心——将成为 2015 年最大的房地产趋势。

paragraphs.sourceText: The report says America’s urbanization will continue to be the most significant issue affecting the industry, as cities across the country imitate the walkability and transit-oriented development making cities like New York and San Francisco so successful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 报告称，美国的城市化仍将是影响该行业的最重要问题，因为全国各地的城市都在模仿步行性和以交通为导向的发展，使得纽约和旧金山等城市如此成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: As smaller cities copy the model of these “24-hour cities，’’ tfiore affordable versions of these places will be created. The report refers to this as the coming of the “18-hour city，”，and uses the term to refer to cities like Houston, Austin, Charlotte, and Nashville, which are “positioning themselves as highly competitive, in terms of livability, employment offerings, and recreational and cultural facilities.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着较小的城市复制这些“24小时城市”的模式，这些地方将被创造出更多经济实惠的版本。报告将其称为“18小时城市”的到来，并用这个词来指代休斯顿、奥斯汀、夏洛特和纳什维尔等城市，这些城市“在宜居性、就业机会、娱乐和文化设施方面将自己定位为极具竞争力”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another trend that looks significant in 2015 is that America’s largest population group, Millennials (千禧一代)，will continue to put off buying a house. Apartments will retain their appeal for a while for Millennials, haunted by what happened to home-owning parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2015年另一个看起来很重要的趋势是，美国最大的人口群体千禧一代将继续推迟买房。对于千禧一代来说，公寓将在一段时间内保留其吸引力，因为他们对拥有住房的父母的遭遇感到困扰。

paragraphs.sourceText: This trend will continue into the 2020s, the report projects. After that, survey respondents disagree over whether this generation will follow in their parents，footsteps, moving to the suburbs to raise families, or will choose to remain in the city center.
paragraphs.translationZh: 报告预计，这一趋势将持续到 2020 年代。此后，受访者对于这一代人是否会追随父母的脚步，搬到郊区养家糊口，还是选择留在市中心，意见不一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another issue affecting real estate in the coming year will be America’s failing infrastructure. Most roads, bridges, transit, water systems, the electric grid, and communications networks were installed 50 to 100 years ago, and they are largely taken for granted until they fail.
paragraphs.translationZh: 明年影响房地产的另一个问题将是美国失败的基础设施。大多数道路、桥梁、交通、供水系统、电网和通信网络都是 50 到 100 年前安装的，在它们失效之前，人们基本上认为它们是理所当然的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The report’s writers state that America’s failure to invest in infrastructure impacts not only the health of the real-estate market, but also our ability to remain globally competitive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该报告的作者指出，美国未能投资基础设施不仅影响房地产市场的健康，而且影响我们保持全球竞争力的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Apart from the specific trends highlighted above, which cause some investors to worry, the report portrays an overall optimism borne by the recent healthy real-estate “upcycle” and improving economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了上述强调的导致一些投资者担忧的具体趋势外，报告还描绘了近期健康的房地产“升级周期”和经济改善所带来的整体乐观情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: Seventy-four percent of the respondents surveyed report a “good to excellent” expectation of real-estate profitability in 2015. While excessive optimism can promote bad investment patterns, resulting in a real-estate “bubble,” the report’s writers downplay that potential outcome in that it has not yet occurred.
paragraphs.translationZh: 74% 的受访者对 2015 年房地产盈利能力的预期为“从好到优秀”。虽然过度乐观可能会促进不良投资模式，导致房地产“泡沫”，但报告作者淡化了这种潜在结果，因为这种结果尚未发生。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The brain is a seemingly endless library, whose shelves house our most precious memories as well as our lifetime’s knowledge. But is there a point where it reaches capacity?
paragraphs.translationZh: 大脑是一个看似无穷无尽的图书馆，它的书架上存放着我们最珍贵的记忆以及我们一生的知识。但是否存在达到容量上限的点呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: The answer is no, because brains are more sophisticated than that. Instead of just crowding in, old 第6 页共8 页 information is sometimes pushed out of the brain for new memories to form.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答案是否定的，因为大脑比这更复杂。旧的信息有时会被推出大脑，以形成新的记忆，而不是仅仅挤入大脑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Previous behavioural studies have shown that learning new information can lead to forgetting. But in a new study, researchers demonstrated for the first time how this effect occurs in the brain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 先前的行为研究表明，学习新信息可能会导致遗忘。但在一项新的研究中，研究人员首次证明了这种效应是如何在大脑中发生的。

paragraphs.sourceText: In daily life, forgetting actually has clear advantages. Imagine, for instance, that you lost your bank card. The new card you receive will come with a new personal identificatipn number (PIN). Each time you remember the new PIN, you gradually forget the old one. This process improves access to relevant information, without old memories interfering.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在日常生活中，遗忘实际上有明显的好处。例如，想象一下您丢失了银行卡。您收到的新卡将附有新的个人识别码 (PIN)。每次记住新的 PIN 码时，您就会逐渐忘记旧的 PIN 码。这个过程可以改善对相关信息的访问，而不会受到旧记忆的干扰。

paragraphs.sourceText: And most of us may sometimes feel the frustration of having old memories interfere with new, relevant memories. Consider trying to remember where you parked your car in the same car park you were at a week earlier. This type of memory (where you are trying to remember new, but similar information) is particularly vulnerable to interference.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们大多数人有时可能会因为旧记忆干扰新的相关记忆而感到沮丧。考虑尝试记住一周前您将车停在同一停车场的位置。这种类型的记忆（您试图记住新的但相似的信息）特别容易受到干扰。

paragraphs.sourceText: When we acquire new information, the brain automatically tries to incorporate ( 合并)it within existing information by forming associations. And when we retrieve (检索) information, both the desired and associated but irrelevant information is recalled.,
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们获取新信息时，大脑会自动尝试通过形成关联将其合并到现有信息中。当我们检索（检索）信息时，所需的信息和相关但不相关的信息都会被回忆起来。

paragraphs.sourceText: The majority of previous research has focused on how we learn and remember new information. But current studies are beginning to place greater emphasis on the conditions under which we forget, as its importance begins to be more appreciated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 之前的大部分研究都集中在我们如何学习和记住新信息。但当前的研究开始更加重视我们遗忘的条件，因为它的重要性开始得到更多的认识。

paragraphs.sourceText: A very small number of people are able to remember almost every detail of their life. While it may sound like an advantage to many, people with this rare condition often find their unusual ability burdensome.
paragraphs.translationZh: 极少数人能够记住他们生活中的几乎每一个细节。虽然这对许多人来说听起来像是一个优势，但患有这种罕见疾病的人常常发现他们不寻常的能力是一种负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a sense, forgetting is our brain’s way of sorting memories, so the most relevant memories are ready for retrieval. Normal forgetting may even be a safety mechanism to ensure our brain doesn’t become too full.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从某种意义上说，遗忘是我们大脑对记忆进行排序的方式，因此最相关的记忆已准备好供检索。正常的遗忘甚至可能是一种安全机制，以确保我们的大脑不会变得太满。
